data_findings: Accepted conversion: South demand is 1.2 tonnes = 1200 kg.
Accepted total point demand is 1800 + 1200 = 3000 kg (3.0 tonnes).
The labor limit permits at most floor(8 / 1.5) = 5 whole loaded trips.
Five full trips provide 5 × 600 = 3000 kg and consume 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 crew-hours.
Allocation trace: North receives 3 trips = 1800 kg; South receives 2 trips = 1200 kg.
One trip remains unused; loading six trips would consume 9 crew-hours and violate the 8 crew-hour limit.
Controllable decisions are the number of trips assigned to each shelter and whether each available trip is used; shelter requests and rainfall are not controllable.
Unit summary row: North | 1800 kg | 1.8 tonnes | 3 trips; South | 1200 kg | 1.2 tonnes | 2 trips; Total | 3000 kg | 3.0 tonnes | 5 trips.
experiment_design: Before dispatch, a second team member independently verifies 1.2 tonnes = 1200 kg and reconciles shelter demand to 3000 kg total.
Count and weigh sealed packs assigned to each of five loads; verify each load is at most 600 kg and shelter totals are exactly 1800 kg North and 1200 kg South.
Reconcile the manifest to three North trips and two South trips, with no sixth loaded trip.
Recalculate loading labor as 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 crew-hours and compare it with the 8 crew-hour roster limit.
Record check results and evidence on the dispatch manifest; hold dispatch on any discrepancy.
falsification_tests: Reject the allocation if an independent conversion does not yield South = 1200 kg or total demand = 3000 kg.
Reject any load whose measured mass exceeds 600 kg.
Reject the manifest if North is not assigned 1800 kg over three trips or South is not assigned 1200 kg over two trips.
Reject the schedule if it loads more than five trips or exceeds 8 crew-hours.
Reject any claimed rainfall-based numerical demand adjustment unless a defensible response model and evidence are supplied.

human_gates: Task-1 gate: an authorized reviewer accepts the metric conversion and point-demand interpretation before task 2 is used.
Pre-dispatch gate: the dispatch lead verifies pack weights/counts, shelter totals, manifest destinations, truck payloads, and crew-hour schedule, then signs the manifest.
Fail-closed rule: any missing evidence or failed check holds dispatch for correction and revalidation.
Any rainfall contingency or demand uplift requires an authorized decision because it is not derivable from the supplied data.
reality_constraints: North requests 1800 kg and South requests 1.2 tonnes for the next 12 hours.
Each trip carries at most 0.6 tonnes (600 kg), and no more than six trips are available.
Each loaded trip consumes 1.5 crew-hours, with at most 8 crew-hours in the shift.
Rainfall is forecast at 75 mm, is not controllable, and may affect demand uncertainty.
Historical attendance is correlated with rainfall, but the brief supplies no causal study.
The individual masses and counts of sealed packs, travel durations, route constraints, and unloading labor are not supplied.
